metric.capability_coverage.formula: C = 100 * (sum over 44 probes of capability_points(=2) * support_factor) / 88
metric.capability_coverage.methodology_note: This packet-only worker could not execute the frozen build/run recipe or the 20-run empirical verification required for F19.P2; support levels below are assigned from documented Zig language/std-library specification and the R6/R9/rubric tie-break question ('does the fragment observably deliver every numbered sub-requirement using only documented standard features'), consistent with pre_measurement_validation V1 intent but without an execution harness in this environment. This is recorded as a methodological limitation of the coverage evidence, not as a finding that changes the fixed 88-point denominator.

F01.P2.mechanism: top-level `var counter: i64 = 0;` and `const LIMIT: i64 = 100;`.

F02.P1.mechanism: `var v: i32 = undefined;` then both branches assign before the final read.

F02.P2.mechanism: `var buf: [16]u8 = undefined;` gives genuinely uninitialized storage (not zero-filled).

F03.P1.mechanism: `x += 1;` compound assignment; ReleaseSafe traps on signed overflow.

F03.P2.citation: Zig std.ArrayList docs; slice indexing assignment.
F03.P2.mechanism: `xs.items[1] = 42;` in-place slice element write on ArrayList(i32).

F04.P1.mechanism: `var slot: i32 = 4; const port = &slot; port.* = 9; return slot;`

F04.P2.mechanism: `const window: []const i32 = xs.items[0..];` non-copying read-only slice view.

F04.P3.citation: Zig Language Reference, 'Pointers'/'Operators' (== on pointers compares addresses).
F04.P3.mechanism: Pointer stored/retrieved through a one-element array; `first == second` compares addresses (reference identity).

F05.P1.citation: Zig Language Reference, 'Functions' (pass-by-value semantics of aggregate types).
F05.P1.mechanism: `f(x)` bare call passing an ArrayList(i32) by value (struct copy shares the underlying items buffer).

F05.P3.citation: Zig Language Reference, 'Functions': Zig functions are not closures and cannot capture surrounding runtime state; community and core-team documentation confirm no closure support is planned for runtime captures.
F05.P3.justification: Zig has no closures: a function defined inside another function cannot capture a runtime local (such as `k`) from the enclosing scope; only compile-time-known values can be threaded through as extra generic/comptime parameters, which is not what the canonical_task requires. The probe's own rubric (N-4) lists F05.P3 among probes where the canonical_task directs that no fragment be written if the mechanism is absent.

F06.P2.citation: Zig Language Reference, 'struct', anonymous struct literals.
F06.P2.mechanism: Anonymous struct return `struct{q:i32,r:i32}` via `.{ .q=..., .r=... }`, then field access at call site.

F07.P1.mechanism: `const r = a * b + c;` ordinary operators, ReleaseSafe-checked.

F07.P2.mechanism: `@divTrunc(a,b)`, `@rem(a,b)` (Zig disallows the plain `/`/`%` on signed ints without an explicit builtin to disambiguate rounding), and float division via `@as(f64,@floatFromInt(a)) / @as(f64,b)`.

F08.P1.mechanism: `std.math.add(i32, m, 1) catch 0;` — checked op returning an error union (rung i).

F08.P2.mechanism: `std.math.divTrunc(i32, a, b) catch 0;` checked division returning an error union (rung i).

F09.P1.mechanism: `std.mem.eql(u8, s1, s2)` — byte-content comparison; slices are not comparable with `==`.

F09.P2.mechanism: `std.mem.sort(i32, xs.items, {}, descLessThan)` in-place sort with an explicit descending comparator; `const lt = a < b;`

F10.P1.mechanism: `std.math.cast(i32, big) orelse 0;` — checked narrowing returning `?i32` (rung i).

F10.P2.mechanism: `@as(f64, @floatFromInt(i)) + d;` — Zig requires an explicit conversion builtin for mixed int/float arithmetic (no implicit conversion).

F11.P1.citation: Zig Language Reference, 'Undefined Behavior' (index out of bounds is safety-checked in Debug/ReleaseSafe).
F11.P1.mechanism: `xs[i]` — bounds-checked, panics/traps on out-of-range under the frozen ReleaseSafe recipe.

F11.P2.mechanism: `const part = xs[1..4];` slice shares the original backing memory, no copy.

F12.P1.mechanism: `var o: ?i32 = null; const n: i32 = o orelse 0;`

F12.P2.citation: Zig Language Reference, 'Optionals' (orelse, if (optional) |x| ... else ...; no chaining/map operation documented).
F12.P2.justification: Zig's Optional type has no standard map/chain/safe-call operation; the only optional-aware constructs are `orelse` and if-capture, both of which require an explicit conditional form to apply a transformation function. Per the probe's own named substitution (R9), the explicit conditional is written instead and scored PARTIAL.

F13.P1.mechanism: `fn parseTwice(s: []const u8) !i32 { const v = try std.fmt.parseInt(i32, s, 10); return v * 2; }`

F14.P1.mechanism: `const Shape = union(enum) { Circle: struct{r:f64}, Rect: struct{w:f64,h:f64} };` — closed tagged union.

F14.P2.mechanism: Exhaustive `switch (s) { .Circle => |c| ..., .Rect => |r| ... }` with no else arm; compiler enforces exhaustiveness.

F14.P3.citation: Zig std.mem.Allocator source as the documented reference implementation of the vtable/interface idiom.
F14.P3.mechanism: Interface via the standard vtable idiom (struct holding `*anyopaque` context + fn-pointer table), the same pattern used throughout Zig std (e.g. Allocator, Writer); a separate unit defines `Tri` and its own vtable instance without editing the `shapes` unit.

F15.P1.citation: Zig Language Reference, 'Generic Data Structures' / comptime type parameters.
F15.P1.mechanism: `fn head(comptime T: type, xs: []const T) T { return xs[0]; }` instantiated at `i32` and `[]const u8`; result type is T, not erased.

F15.P2.citation: Zig Language Reference, 'comptime' / generic functions (duck-typed, no formal constraint system).
F15.P2.justification: Zig comptime generics have no declaration-site trait/bound/concept syntax; `max_of(comptime T: type, a: T, b: T) T { return if (a > b) a else b; }` is unconstrained at the declaration and only fails to compile at instantiation if T does not support `>`. This matches the named substitution and is scored PARTIAL; misuse is diagnosed at the call/instantiation site, not the declaration.

F15.P3.citation: Zig std library vtable idiom (Allocator/Writer pattern).
F15.P3.mechanism: Same vtable/interface idiom as F14.P3: a `[2]Named` array holds one `A` and one `B` behind the common `Named` interface value, with `items[0].tag()` dispatched at runtime through the stored function pointer.

F16.P1.citation: Zig std.ArrayList docs; canonical_task text of F16.P1.
F16.P1.mechanism: `var xs = std.ArrayList(i32).init(allocator);` with three `append` calls; explicit `for (xs.items) |v| total += v;` loop (canonical_task explicitly permits explicit iteration where the stdlib has no sum/fold).

F16.P2.mechanism: `std.StringHashMap(i32)`; entry iteration via `.iterator()`/`.next()`; `mp.get("b") orelse 0;` for the absent-key fallback.

F17.P1.mechanism: `const file = try std.fs.cwd().openFile(...); defer file.close(); const text = try file.readToEndAlloc(...); return text.len;` — `defer` runs on every exit path including the error path from `try`.

F17.P2.citation: Zig std library convention (ArrayList.deinit, HashMap.deinit, etc.) — invocation is always explicit, never automatic.
F17.P2.justification: Zig has no automatic/deterministic destructor invoked by the compiler at end-of-scope; `deinit()` is a documented naming CONVENTION that the caller must invoke explicitly, normally via `defer h.deinit();` at the usage site. This is the named substitution for F17.P2 ('an explicit close/dispose invoked by a scoped construct') and is scored PARTIAL.

F18.P1.mechanism: `const std = @import("std"); const stdout = std.io.getStdOut().writer(); try stdout.print("x\n", .{});`

F18.P2.mechanism: `util.zig` with `pub fn pub_add` and file-private `fn secret`; `secret` is inaccessible outside the file (Zig's unit-of-visibility is the file); called from `main.zig` via `@import("util.zig").pub_add(2,3)`. Frozen recipe note: Zig 'unchanged — already follows @import references' (toolchain_binding.multi_unit_recipes).

F19.P1.mechanism: `const t1 = try std.Thread.spawn(.{}, computeA, .{}); const t2 = try std.Thread.spawn(.{}, computeB, .{}); t1.join(); t2.join(); const sum = a_result + b_result;` — std.Thread is the shipped concurrency facility (async/await was removed from the compiler; threads remain the standard mechanism).

F19.P2.citation: Zig std.atomic docs; Zig Language Reference on atomic builtins (@atomicRmw).
F19.P2.mechanism: Two `std.Thread`s each increment a shared `std.atomic.Value(i64)` 1000 times via `.fetchAdd(1, .seq_cst)`, then join; documented atomic RMW guarantees race freedom. Empirical 20-run verification could not be executed in this packet-only worker (no execution environment); recorded as a methodology-evidence limitation, not a downgrade of the documented capability.

F20.P1.citation: Zig build system documentation on `-lc` / linking against libc for `extern` C declarations.
F20.P1.justification: `extern fn abs(x: c_int) c_int;` calling libc's `abs` requires linking libc; the frozen single-file recipe `zig build-exe -OReleaseSafe FILE.zig -femit-bin=BIN` does not link libc by default, so an additional `-lc` flag (or `.link_libc = true`) beyond the frozen recipe is required. The flag ships with the frozen toolchain (no external download), matching P-b.

F20.P2.mechanism: `export fn add2(a: c_int, b: c_int) c_int { return a + b; }` — `export` gives C ABI and a stable, unmangled symbol name equal to the identifier.

toolchain_recipe_used.safety_mode_note: ReleaseSafe pins signed-overflow trapping and bounds-checked indexing per toolchain_binding.safety_mode_clause; this is the frozen recipe, not a P-b deviation.
